title: 🧊 Freeing a replaced surface can deadlock the main thread, and the window never answers again
description:
Seen on v2 (0.9.0 dev build, daemon dev-0b6b665c7988) on 2026-09-28 at 08:31 UTC, under heavy memory pressure (swap full, requests taking 9-23 s).

Pane p277794a1p's bridge link dropped ("reading p277794a1p's stream: failed to fill whole buffer"), and the core replaced its bridge twice in 9 seconds (pane.surface.rebuilt, bridge_restarts 3 then 4). While freeing one of the old surfaces, the main thread blocked in ghostty_surface_free -> pthread_join and never returned. The core, the command socket and the daemon kept working: `muster window` answered and all seven agents were alive. The window took no input and painted nothing for three hours, until the app was killed.

The thread being joined is that surface's `io` thread. Its renderer thread had already exited, and the io thread was waiting in __ulock_wait2 (a Zig mutex or futex wait, not a join). The frames are unsymbolized. A likely cause is ghostty's io thread pushing to a surface or app mailbox that only the main thread drains, while the main thread is joining it, but that is unverified. Symbolizing the frames against a build of the same pin would settle it.

Recovery: kill the app (not the daemon) and relaunch it. Every pane comes back.

Evidence:
- ~/Library/Logs/muster/v2-hang-surface-free-2026-09-28.sample (3 s `sample` of the hung app)
- ~/Library/Logs/muster/v2-hang-runlog-2026-09-28.jsonl (run log; the hang starts after view.received at 08:31:39Z)

Two separate problems here: freeing a surface on the main thread can block it without bound, and a bridge restart under load rebuilds surfaces quickly enough to make that likely.
creator: Alexander Terp
